annotations.note: 9M26 net debt rose to TRY 149.7bn (from TRY 133bn YE25) with compressed Q3 EBITDA (~TRY 3.47bn) on weak soda ash & glass prices.
Producer is positioned in the bottom quartile (Q1) of global production costs, preserving positive EBITDA generation across cyclical commodity troughs.
>75% of revenues billed in USD/EUR against predominantly local-currency operating expenditures, creating a structural natural FX hedge.
Controls world-class mineral or petrochemical reserves essential to the domestic economy, ensuring sovereign backstop support in stress scenarios.
Q326 EBITDA plunged 61.2% YoY to TRY 3,466m (5.2% margin); 9M26 EBITDA TRY 13,032m (-38.3% YoY, 6.7% margin) on soda ash & European glass weakness.

verdict.stance: Underweight / Severe Soda Ash & Glass Margin Contraction (5.2% Q3 Margin)
verdict.summary: Şişecam's credit metrics remained under cyclically severe pressure in 9M26 as weak European flat-glass and global soda-ash pricing compressed Q3 EBITDA (~TRY 3.47bn) and lifted net debt to TRY 149.7bn (from TRY 133bn at YE25). İşbank parentage and US natural soda ash assets mitigate downside.

positives: Global top-tier market position across flat glass, glassware, glass packaging, and natural soda ash (Wyoming).
Diversified international revenue base (~60% ex-Türkiye / export) and strong İşbank parentage.
negatives: Sharp earnings collapse: Q326 EBITDA -61.2% YoY to TRY 3.47bn (5.2% margin vs 12.8% Q325); 9M EBITDA -38.3% YoY.
Persistent global soda ash oversupply and weak European construction/automotive glass demand.
Leverage creeping upward as FCF softens alongside multi-year capex.
